documents.title: Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: The page says "Most professors will include specific rules" and "many faculty may encourage or even require the use of AI, others may prohibit it", so it sets no uniform stance and defers to instructors, with a default of no AI absent authorization.
documents.summary: Student-facing academic-integrity statement: AI is a learning aid, but students follow instructor rules, must attribute AI content, understand what they submit and respect copyright. Unauthorized AI-generated work may violate the conduct code.

units.why: The opening frames the statement as a values preamble: "NJIT values academic integrity and ethical behavior in all learning activities, including using artificial intelligence (AI) tools". It sets purpose and principles for all, so P56 (framework) fits, not a rule type.
units.anchor: NJIT values academic integrity and ethical behavior in all learning activities

units.why: "AI can help students develop new skills and improve student learning outcomes" states a benefit of AI for learning; it informs rather than directs, so P44 (effective AI use as a skill), informs, permit-leaning.
units.anchor: AI can help students develop new skills and improve student learning outcomes

units.why: "students must adhere to the expectations outlined by their instructors" binds students to whatever the instructor sets, i.e. the rule is set per instructor (P04). Must, student.
units.anchor: students must adhere to the expectations outlined by their instructors

units.why: "not utilize these tools to conduct or support academic dishonesty such as cheating and plagiarism" bans AI use for dishonesty and ties it to cheating/plagiarism, so P36 (misconduct) rather than P19 since it does not speak of generating submitted work.
units.anchor: not utilize these tools to conduct or support academic dishonesty

units.why: "Most professors will include specific rules regarding AI use in their course syllabus" describes where rules are communicated; it is an informs statement about syllabus statements (P09).
units.anchor: Most professors will include specific rules regarding AI use in their course syllabus

units.why: "These rules may vary across professors, courses, and even individual assignments" and "may encourage or even require ... others may prohibit" says the stance is decided per instructor and assignment (P04).
units.anchor: These rules may vary across professors, courses, and even individual assignments

units.why: "If a student has not received explicit authorization ... submitting AI generated work may constitute a violation" gives the default when permission is absent: AI-generated work is not allowed unless authorized. P06 (fallback) is chosen over P36 because the core is the default-when-silent rule; misconduct is secondary.
units.anchor: If a student has not received explicit authorization from their course instructor to use AI

units.why: "it is crucial to carefully review the syllabus and seek clarification from the professor when it is unclear" tells students to check and ask when unsure: P10, should.
units.anchor: carefully review the syllabus and seek clarification from the professor when it is unclear

units.why: "students must ensure that their work remains original" requires submitted work to be the student's own: P29 (ownership), must.
units.anchor: students must ensure that their work remains original

units.why: "giving credit to the authors or sources of any ideas ... whether generated in whole or in part by AI" requires attribution of AI-generated content: P24 (disclose with submission), must.
units.anchor: giving credit to the authors or sources of any ideas, quotes, or information

units.why: The parenthetical examples "Grammarly, Quillbot, Claude.ai" and "GitHub, Integrated Development Environment Software" define which tools count as AI or external sources for attribution, setting the policy scope: P61.
units.anchor: Grammarly, Quillbot, Claude.ai, etc.
units.policy: Tools such as Grammarly, Quillbot, Claude.ai, and external sources such as GitHub and IDE software are within the scope of required attribution.

units.why: "students should exercise critical thinking skills ... critically evaluate" asks students to evaluate AI content; P31 (verify/evaluate), should.
units.anchor: students should exercise critical thinking skills when using AI-generated content

units.why: "Submitting AI-generated work as a student's own without giving proper credit ... is unacceptable" makes undisclosed AI submission the violation, so P28 (nondisclosure is the violation) fits better than P19 since credit would cure it.
units.anchor: Submitting AI-generated work as a student's own without giving proper credit
units.policy: Submitting AI-generated work as a student's own without giving proper credit is unacceptable.

units.why: "relying on AI to complete assignments without understanding the content is unacceptable" requires students to understand what they submit: P30.
units.anchor: relying on AI to complete assignments without understanding the content is unacceptable
units.policy: Relying on AI to complete assignments without understanding the content is unacceptable.

units.why: "students must adhere to copyright laws and intellectual property rights when utilizing AI tools" is an IP obligation: P52, must.
units.anchor: students must adhere to copyright laws and intellectual property rights

units.why: "Students should not use AI to duplicate or alter copyrighted materials without permission" restricts a specific AI use on copyrighted works: P52 (copyright), should-not.
units.anchor: Students should not use AI to duplicate or alter copyrighted materials without permission
units.policy: Students should not use AI to duplicate or alter copyrighted materials without permission.

units.why: The note that the statement "was developed with assistance from ChatGPT and Grammarly" discloses the institution's own AI use in drafting, a transparency statement: P47 (disclosing AI use by staff), informs.
units.anchor: developed with assistance from ChatGPT and Grammarly

documents.unit: Emerging Technologies / AI Teaching and Learning Working Group
documents.title: Instructor Autonomy (NJIT's perspective on AI usage in teaching/learning)
documents.stance_why: "instructors should have autonomy in developing specific policies within their courses" and the page offers three pathways (prohibition, conditional, free) rather than one rule, so it delegates.
documents.summary: Institution perspective page giving instructors autonomy, with guidance on ethics, bias, citation, detection, equity and data, plus three sample syllabus tiers and support resources.

units.why: "instructors should have autonomy in developing specific policies within their courses" leaves the rule to instructors: P04, should.
units.anchor: instructors should have autonomy in developing specific policies within their courses

units.why: "NJIT's perspective on AI is to foster intellectual development, critical thinking, and to uphold academic integrity" states institution-level principles: P56.
units.anchor: NJIT's perspective on AI is to foster intellectual development, critical thinking

units.why: "prepare students to excel in a workforce where AI plays an increasingly significant role" is a career rationale: P44.
units.anchor: prepare students to excel in a workforce where AI plays an increasingly significant role

units.why: "these tools are not shortcuts to bypass the learning process but tools to advance it" defines responsible use as not shortcutting learning: P41.
units.anchor: these tools are not shortcuts to bypass the learning process but tools to advance it

units.why: "Using content ... not written by oneself and sharing it as one's work is considered plagiarism" classes unattributed use as plagiarism, unless cited or permitted: P36.
units.anchor: sharing it as one's work is considered plagiarism

units.why: "Unless cited or permitted by one's instructor, the university emphasizes this concept of plagiarism" conditions use on citation or instructor permission: P24 disclosure, though P36 also fits; chosen P24 because the cure is citation.
units.anchor: Unless cited or permitted by one's instructor

units.why: The copyright definition "Provides exclusive rights to human authors to protect the work they've created" explains copyright as a consideration: P52, informs.
units.anchor: Provides exclusive rights to human authors to protect the work

units.why: The AI Bias definition "potential for AI systems to exhibit unfair or discriminatory behavior" names bias as a concern: P53.
units.anchor: potential for AI systems to exhibit unfair or discriminatory behavior

units.why: "Read sources cited by AI, instead of just using them" is a mitigation recommendation to verify AI output: P31, should.
units.anchor: Read sources cited by AI, instead of just using them.

units.why: "compare information from multiple sources" is another recommended verification step against AI misinformation: P31, should.
units.anchor: compare information from multiple sources

units.why: "Citing your AI tool sources is critical when using AI tools" asks for citation of AI: P24, should (recommended, with citation authorities varying).
units.anchor: Citing your AI tool sources is critical when using AI tools

units.why: "supports using plagiarism detection tools, but not as the sole reason" allows detection tools as supporting evidence only: P40 (tools used) chosen over P39 because tools are supported; the limit is in the next unit.
units.anchor: The university supports using plagiarism detection tools
units.policy: The university supports using plagiarism detection tools, but not as the sole reason for going against academic integrity.

units.why: "no AI Detector is 100% accurate" states detectors are unreliable and must not be the sole basis for a violation: P39.
units.anchor: no AI Detector is 100% accurate
units.policy: Detection tools are not the sole reason for going against academic integrity, as no AI Detector is 100% accurate.

units.why: "NJIT recommends that instructors first speak with students regarding any potential violations" is the talk-first step: P57, should.
units.anchor: NJIT recommends that instructors first speak with students

units.why: "NJIT is working to increase its library of AI-licensed tools to decrease the equity gap" addresses unequal access by providing licensed tools: P51 (equity), informs.
units.anchor: NJIT is working to increase its library of AI-licensed tools to decrease the equity gap

units.why: "it is recommended to limit this usage to NJIT-licensed tools" prefers university-licensed tools when AI is opened to students: P50 (prefer vetted) rather than P17, since it limits rather than provides.
units.anchor: it is recommended to limit this usage to NJIT-licensed tools

units.why: "this information should be addressed in a course's syllabus" asks instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus: P09, should.
units.anchor: this information should be addressed in a course's syllabus

units.why: "these applications may collect, store, use, and sell data" warns of data practices of genAI tools: P50 (protect data), informs.
units.anchor: these applications may collect, store, use, and sell data

units.why: "Any AI tool licensed university-wide goes through a security and data vetting process within ... IST" describes institutional review of AI tools: P65, informs.
units.anchor: goes through a security and data vetting process

units.why: "it is recommended that they touch base with IST ... for assistance in vetting" asks instructors to have IST vet tools they want: P50 (prefer vetted tools), should.
units.anchor: it is recommended that they touch base with IST

units.why: "No confidential information should be shared with the AI if it is being trained on the content submitted" bars confidential data: P50, should-not.
units.anchor: No confidential information should be shared with the AI

units.why: "If students are asked to use AI, they will be made aware of what not to do" commits instructors to warn students about data risks: P50, informs.
units.anchor: they will be made aware of what not to do

units.why: The sample syllabus text "avoid sharing personal information (e.g., full name, email address, or location)" is advice to students to protect personal data: P50, should-not.
units.anchor: avoid sharing personal information (e.g., full name, email address

units.why: "three pathways that NJIT instructors may take regarding course policy on AI usage" names tiers (prohibition, conditional, free): P05.
units.anchor: three pathways that NJIT instructors may take regarding course policy

units.why: "it is recommended that every instructor inlude their policy in the syllabi" regardless of stance: P09, should.
units.anchor: it is recommended that every instructor inlude their policy

units.why: "NJIT has provided access to certain AI tools at a university level" states a sanctioned university-provided tool: P17, informs.
units.anchor: NJIT has provided access to certain AI tools at a university level

units.why: "be aware of the equity and data challenges" of non-university tools asks instructors to consider access and data when requiring a tool: P51 chosen over P50 because it leads with equity.
units.anchor: please be aware of the equity and data challenges

units.why: "Focus on developing foundational skills that are not dependent on AI technologies" is a reason given for complete prohibition; it protects fundamentals: P42, informs.
units.anchor: Focus on developing foundational skills that are not dependent on AI technologies

units.why: "Increase equity in a course, as not all AI tools will be available to all students" is a stated reason for prohibition: P51, informs.
units.anchor: Increase equity in a course, as not all AI tools will be available

units.why: The example "AI usage is not permitted throughout this course under any circumstance" is template text for a full ban: P01, offered as an option instructors may adopt.
units.anchor: AI usage is not permitted throughout this course under any circumstance

units.why: "It is not permitted to be used in the following assignments ... X, Y, Z" is template text letting AI be allowed for some assignments and not others: P04 (per-assignment), fits better than P01.
units.anchor: use of artificial intelligence (AI) is permitted in this course for certain assignments

units.why: "the AI must be cited as is shown within the NJIT Library AI citation page" in the conditional template requires citation: P24, must.
units.anchor: the AI must be cited as is shown within the NJIT Library AI

units.why: "reach out to your instructor prior to submitting any assignments" is template text telling students to ask when in doubt: P10, should.
units.anchor: reach out to your instructor prior to submitting any assignments

units.why: "Prepare students for AI usage as a part of their daily responsibilities in the workforce" is a stated reason for conditional permission: P44.
units.anchor: Prepare students for AI usage as a part of their daily responsibilities in the workforce.

units.why: "The usage of artificial intelligence (AI) is permitted in this course and no citation is necessary" is template text for free use: P02.
units.anchor: AI) is permitted in this course and no citation is necessary.

units.why: "it cannot replace human interaction in education. NJIT encourages instructors and departments to increase interactions" recommends course redesign toward interaction: P35, should.
units.anchor: NJIT encourages instructors and departments to increase interactions in their courses

units.why: "NJIT advocates for development opportunities for instructors to adapt" supports faculty learning: P63.
units.anchor: NJIT advocates for development opportunities for instructors to adapt

units.why: "will be updated here when available" says support logistics are under discussion and will be revised: P54, informs.
units.anchor: will be updated here when available

units.why: "students should first work directly with their instructors as a first avenue of support" directs students to the instructor's own policy: P10, should.
units.anchor: students should first work directly with their instructors

documents.title: For Students: Official AI Guide (AI-U 2026)
documents.stance_why: "instructors have the freedom to determine whether or not students are permitted to use generative AI"; the page encourages exploration in general but leaves the decision to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: Student page adopting the 2026 Elon/AAC&U AI-U guide. It welcomes AI for brainstorming, writing clarity and study tools with citation, and sends students to the syllabus and instructor.

units.why: "we encourage students to explore AI technologies to support their studies" sets a welcoming default: P02, encourage.
units.anchor: While we encourage students to explore AI technologies to support their studies

units.why: "instructors have the freedom to determine whether or not students are permitted to use generative AI" hands the decision to instructors: P04.
units.anchor: instructors have the freedom to determine whether or not students are permitted

units.why: "Your first step should always be to check the course syllabus" tells students where to find the rule: P10 (check and ask), should.
units.anchor: Your first step should always be to check the course syllabus

units.why: "you can utilize generative AI for tasks such as brainstorming ideas" permits brainstorming: P15.
units.anchor: brainstorming ideas

units.why: "improving writing clarity" permits AI for prose improvement: P18 (prose separately), may.
units.anchor: improving writing clarity

units.why: "creating study tools" permits AI for study aids: P14, may.
units.anchor: creating study tools

units.why: "emphasizes the importance of citing AI-generated content" says AI content should be cited: P24, should.
units.anchor: the importance of citing AI-generated content

units.why: "always with a commitment to originality, honesty, and fairness in your work" asks students to keep work their own: P29, should.
units.anchor: always with a commitment to originality, honesty, and fairness in your work

units.why: "NJIT has adopted the AI-U Guide Series ... created by Elon University and the AAC&U" adopts an external framework for student guidance: P56.
units.anchor: NJIT has adopted the

units.why: "AI Core Competencies for Students, created as a benchmark for building curriculum" frames AI skills as career preparation: P44, informs.
units.anchor: created as a benchmark for building curriculum that will lead to post-graduation success

units.why: "serving as an update to the previously created guidelines from Spring 2023" shows the guidance is revised over time: P54, informs.
units.anchor: serving as an update to the previously created guidelines from Spring 2023

documents.unit: Emerging Technologies / AI Teaching and Learning Working Group
documents.title: AI Teaching and Learning Working Group
documents.stance_why: The page only describes the working group and lists members; it states no stance, so it falls to delegates by default.
documents.summary: Description of the AI Teaching and Learning Working Group and its membership, with almost no rules.

units.why: "has been working since 2024 to support and guide NJIT's response to AI" describes a standing body maintaining the institution's AI guidance: P56, informs. It sets no rule.
units.anchor: support and guide NJIT's response to AI as it relates to teaching, learning, and curriculum

notes: No school or computing-unit policy collected. Saved texts include site navigation, which was skipped. Template sample text in the Instructor Autonomy page was coded as options instructors may adopt.
